original_question: Fix an embedding dimension e and let F be a family of numerical semigroups with that fixed embedding dimension. For each i = 1, ..., e - 1 define B_i(F) = sup{ b_i(R_Gamma) | Gamma in F }, where R_Gamma is the local semigroup ring of Gamma. Must it be true that the quantities B_i(F) are either all finite or all infinite?
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper’s exact target. It correctly fixes a family of numerical semigroups with common embedding dimension e, defines family-wise suprema of the i-th Betti numbers for i = 1, ..., e-1, and asks for the same dichotomy stated in the paper: whether these suprema must be simultaneously finite or simultaneously infinite.
missing_details: A ground field k should be fixed. In Section 1 the semigroup rings are defined over a field, and the paper notes that intermediate Betti numbers can depend on the characteristic.
The local semigroup ring should be identified explicitly as R_Gamma = k[[Gamma]] = k[[t^{n_1},...,t^{n_e}]] when Gamma = <n_1,...,n_e>.
The meaning of beta_i(R_Gamma) should be stated: it is the i-th Betti number in a minimal free resolution of R_Gamma over a minimal regular local presentation.
It should be explicit that every Gamma in the family has embedding dimension exactly e, not merely at most e.

No extra hypotheses such as symmetry, almost symmetry, width bounds, homogeneity, degree conditions, or nilpotency assumptions belong to this problem; the paper asks it for arbitrary families of numerical semigroups of fixed embedding dimension.
refined_question: Fix a field k and a positive integer e. Let F be a family of numerical semigroups Gamma with embedding dimension e(Gamma) = e. For each Gamma in F, write Gamma = <n_1,...,n_e> and let R_Gamma = k[[Gamma]] = k[[t^{n_1},...,t^{n_e}]] be its local semigroup ring. Let beta_i(R_Gamma) denote the i-th Betti number of R_Gamma over a minimal regular local presentation. For each i = 1, ..., e - 1, define B_i(F) = sup{beta_i(R_Gamma) : Gamma in F}. Is it true that the numbers B_1(F), ..., B_{e-1}(F) are either all finite or all infinite?
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, one may replace R_Gamma = k[[Gamma]] by the graded semigroup ring k[Gamma], since Section 1 states that beta_i(k[[Gamma]]) = beta_i(k[Gamma]) for all i.
justification: This is exactly the open problem stated as Problem 24 in Section 6. Your draft already matches the family-level supremum formulation and the finite-versus-infinite dichotomy in the paper. To make it fully stand-alone and faithful to the paper, the main missing ingredients are the fixed ground field k, the precise ring-theoretic meaning of R_Gamma and of beta_i, and the fact that the paper imposes no extra structural assumptions on the family beyond fixed embedding dimension. The nearby context in Section 6 also explains that the first interesting case is embedding dimension 4 and relates that case to Theorem 17 and Problem 25.
